gaps.sentence: Tell me ___ you said to her.
gaps.explanation: 'What you said' means 'the words that you said'; 'that' cannot head the clause after 'me'.

gaps.sentence: Do you remember the time ___ we got lost in Rome?
gaps.explanation: 'When' introduces defining clauses after 'the time'; 'which' would need a preposition.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ hand in their essays late will lose marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to the students performing the action; the verb 'will lose' follows later in the sentence.
'What caused the fire' means 'the thing that caused it'; 'that' cannot act as the subject of this nominal clause.

gaps.sentence: She has three daughters, all of ___ are at university.
gaps.explanation: 'All of whom' refers to people after 'of'; 'all of which' is for things and 'all of them' cannot join the clauses after a comma.

gaps.sentence: The company's shares, ___ rose sharply yesterday, are still undervalued.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to the shares; 'that' is impossible in a clause set off by commas.

gaps.sentence: July and August are the months ___ most Italians take their holidays.
gaps.explanation: 'When' means 'in which' after time expressions; the clause describes when the action happens.

gaps.sentence: The director, ___ we met at the conference, has written to us.
gaps.hint: person as object, but the clause is non-defining
gaps.explanation: In non-defining clauses 'that' cannot replace 'who', even when the person is the object.
